previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of hepatitis C and alcoholic cirrhosis, was admitted for his second transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) of a recurrent liver tumor. The procedure was performed successfully, after which he developed expected post-embolization symptoms including mild abdominal pain and nausea. On the second hospital day, he experienced rigors and was found to have a new left lower lobe pneumonia on chest X-ray, for which he was started on oral levofloxacin. His liver enzymes rose as expected, and his platelet count remained low but stable. He improved clinically, with resolution of chills and nausea, and was discharged home on day four. He was sent home with a five-day course of antibiotics, continued vancomycin and Florastor for C. difficile prevention, and pain and nausea medications as needed. Follow-up was arranged with his hepatology and transplant teams.

radiology_notes.text:
CT OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

HISTORY:  History of hepatocellular carcinoma, hepatitis C and alcohol status
post prior chemoembolization.  Patient presents with dizziness, abdominal
pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.

COMPARISONS:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis is available from ___ as
well as more recent MRI study from ___ also chest CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
with intravenous contrast.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were also
performed.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN:  Aside from minor atelectasis, the lung bases appear clear.  There
are no pleural effusions.  

The liver has a nodular appearance consistent with cirrhosis.  The patient is
status post cholecystectomy.  A tiny persistent fluid collection in the
gallbladder fossa appears unchanged.  A focus of persistent Ethiodol uptake
can be seen in the left lateral segments of the liver, although other areas
along the lateral segments of the liver have washed-out.  A radiofrequency
ablation zone in the right lobe appears unchanged.  This study is not
optimized for detection of hepatocellular carcinoma.  The adrenal glands and
kidneys appear within normal limits.  The spleen is again enlarged.  The main
portal vein and its major branches appear unchanged.  Large paraesophageal
varices are apparent as well as splenorenal shunting.  Slight thickening of
the colon at the splenic flexure appears unchanged and may be due to portal
hypertension.  The distal colon is underdistended.  Although it is difficult
to exclude inflammation, the appearance is not definitive for colitis.  

CT PELVIS:  The prostate, seminal vesicles and bladder appear within normal
range.  Calcified structures in the mid small bowel mesentery are thought to
represent retained gallstones.  Patchy vascular calcifications are present
without an aneurysm.  There is no ascites or lymphadenopathy.  

BONE WINDOWS:  The bones are probably demineralized to some degree.  There are
no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions.  There is substantial sclerosis along
lower thoracic interspaces, but compatible with a degenerative etiology and
unchanged.  Mild degenerative changes are also noted along the mid-to-lower
lumbar spine without change.

IMPRESSION:  No definite evidence for colitis or other acute process.  The
distal colon is collapsed and difficult to evaluate, however, making it
difficult to completely exclude inflammation.  Washout of some of the Ethiodol
from the background liver in the left lateral segments since the prior study
without other change in cirrhosis, sequelae of portal hypertension, or prior
procedure-related changes in the liver.
